correctness_confidence.basis: The proof elegantly combines commutative algebra (valuation rings, specialization) with explicit Clifford conjugations to reduce the operator rank problem to Frenkel's polynomial lemma. The logic is flawless and heavily verified by exact certificates.

rigor.basis: The author meticulously handles field extensions, localizations, and residue characteristics. The distinction between algebraic proofs and numerical/exact certificates is impeccably maintained throughout the text.

novelty.basis: The core insight—that the non-unimodular Clifford conjugations F'Q_s preserve the support and exact coefficients of a Weyl combination up to phases, enabling a valuation-based pigeonhole argument—is highly original and brilliantly applied.

significance.basis: Establishes a fundamental sparsity-rank law for Weyl operators in prime dimensions, decisively solving the optimal list decoding problem for pure probes of given Schmidt rank and extending the Chebotarev-Tao theorem.

reproducibility.basis: The computational evidence is exhaustively detailed, explicitly distinguishing finite-precision searches from exact algebraic certificates. Complete Python scripts and data are provided and clearly documented.

summary: This manuscript proves a fundamental Weyl sparsity-nullity law for matrices in prime dimensions: any linear combination of ℓ Weyl operators has nullity at most ℓ-1. This brilliantly generalizes the Chebotarev-Tao uncertainty principle from vectors to operators. The proof uses a specialization and valuation ring reduction, cleverly employing specific non-unimodular Clifford conjugations that preserve the exact coefficients (up to phases) to execute a pigeonhole principle across all p+1 lines in the phase space. The paper further applies this law to establish the exact minimal list length for quantum list decoding with pure probes of a given Schmidt rank, tightly closing an open problem in the literature. Additionally, it refutes the intuitive "line conjecture" with an exact, verified counterexample on a parabola in p=5. The mathematical exposition is remarkably concise, rigorous, and beautifully supported by exhaustive exact and numerical verification scripts.
strengths: Masterful synthesis of commutative algebra (valuation rings) and quantum information (Clifford group, Weyl operators) to yield a short, definitive proof.
Solves a clear, foundational open problem regarding Pauli/Weyl operator ranks in prime dimensions.
Provides a complete, exact refutation of the natural "line conjecture".
Flawless integration of rigorous mathematical proof with extensive, well-documented computational certificates.
weaknesses: The mathematical exposition is highly dense; the rapid transition through the specialization lemma, valuation rings, and Clifford conjugations requires significant mathematical maturity from the reader.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact structural observation that U_s = F'Q_s preserves the coefficients of a Weyl combination up to p-th roots of unity, enabling a reduction-modulo-p argument across all directions despite the non-unimodularity of the Fourier matrix.
The theorem rank(C) + s_W(C) ≥ p+1, successfully generalizing the Chebotarev-Tao principle to non-commutative operators.
